question: If A, B and C are arbitrary events, then P (A ∩ B ∩ C) equals to:
solution:
The correct answer is** ****P(A) P(B | A)P(C | A∩B)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The symbol ∩ represents the intersection of events, meaning "and".
 
• The probability of the intersection of events A, B, and C (A ∩ B ∩ C) is equal to the probability of A times the conditional probability of B given A times the conditional probability of C given the intersection of A and B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **conditional probability **ofB given A (P (B | A)) represents the probability of event B occurring given that event A has occurred.
 
• The **conditional probability **of C given the intersection of A and B (P (C | A ∩ B)) represents the probability of event C occurring given that both events A and B have occurred.
 
• This formula represents the chain rule of probability, which states that the probability of multiple events occurring in a certain order is equal to the product of their individual probabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Understanding the **chain rule of probability** and the **concept of conditional probability** is important in various fields, including statistics and computer science.
 
• The formula P (A ∩ B ∩ C) = P (A) P (B | A) P (C | A ∩ B) is widely used in decision making, particularly in risk analysis and game theory.
 
• Careful application of the chain rule is crucial in avoiding incorrect calculations and reaching incorrect conclusions.
